Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presentation: 40-year-old with 2 days of wheeze and shortness of breath beginning about an hour after heavy dust exposure during house cleaning; worse at night; at times unable to complete sentences. No chest pain with deep inspiration, no dizziness. History of childhood asthma (exercise-triggered symptoms persist), seasonal hay fever, prior steroid use for asthma. Has an inhaler from a few months ago; has not used it for this episode. No current antihistamines at home.
- Most consistent with an acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by dust/allergen exposure, with consideration of irritant-induced bronchospasm. DDx from diagnostic reasoning aligns with transcript.
- Plan per consultation:
  - Attend in-person clinic/GP today for assessment and tests, including pulse oximetry to assess oxygen saturation.
  - Consider antihistamine (over-the-counter) en route or to be prescribed if needed.
  - Steroids may be required depending on in-person assessment.
  - Clinician to send a letter to GP summarizing the consultation.

Management Plan
- Immediate in-person evaluation at GP/clinic for wheeze and dyspnea
- Pulse oximetry to assess oxygen saturation; further tests as determined in clinic
- Consider trial of antihistamine (OTC) prior to visit if accessible; otherwise obtain via GP
- Possible steroid treatment if indicated after assessment
- Letter to GP provided via app for same-day review

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by dust/allergen exposure – High likelihood. Justified by atopic history (hay fever), prior asthma with residual exercise-induced symptoms, onset after dust exposure, nocturnal worsening, and wheeze limiting speech.
- Irritant-induced bronchospasm from dust/cleaning exposure – Moderate likelihood. Temporal relationship to heavy dust exposure without infectious prodrome supports.
- Allergic rhinitis with lower-airway involvement (dust mite allergy leading to bronchospasm) – Moderate likelihood. Atopic background and dust exposure consistent; nasal symptoms not reported.
